Maintenance Report — MNT-0174-003

Asset: WELL-0174 (NE-08 Well 174, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 20 May 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0174-0031 on 2023-05-18 Report written: 21 May 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0174-0031 at 10:45 on 2023-05-18 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.0% of the pad area, estimated 2.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 294 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 235 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0174-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.41% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0174-008

Asset: WELL-0174 (NE-08 Well 174, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 29 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 30 Oct 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 39 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0174-0053 on 2023-10-26 Report written: 31 Oct 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0174-0053 showed the wellhead at 27.7 °C with the air at 19.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0174-017

Asset: WELL-0174 (NE-08 Well 174, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jan 2025 08:00 · Finished: 27 Jan 2025 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 37 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0174-0116 on 2025-01-23 Report written: 28 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0174-0116 showed the wellhead at 12.4 °C with the air at 10.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0174-017 (WS-06).
